note: Singularity: something unusual. It refers to Billy’s body showing no movement when hanged.

anchor: the Purser, a rather ruddy rotund person
note: The purser kept the ship’s accounts and sold sailors clothes and tobacco. Rotund: round and plump.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Purser”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: What testimony to the force lodged in will-power
note: Testimony: evidence. The purser takes Billy’s stillness as proof of the power of will.
Saturnine: gloomy, bitter in temperament, like the planet Saturn’s supposed influence.

anchor: any movement following the completed suspension
note: Suspension: here, hanging by the neck.

anchor: mechanical spasm in the muscular system
a term not yet included in the lexicon of science
note: Lexicon: dictionary, the vocabulary of a field.

anchor: the hypothesis that at the first touch of the halyards
note: Hypothesis: a proposed explanation to be tested. Halyards are the ropes that hoist sails, here the hangman’s rope.
Pertinaciously: stubbornly, refusing to give up.

anchor: was it a species of euthanasia
note: Euthanasia: an easy, painless death. The word is from Greek for “good death.”

anchor: It is at once imaginative and metaphysical—in short, Greek
note: The surgeon distrusts the word as vague philosophy. Metaphysical: concerned with abstract matters.
The sick-bay was the ship’s hospital, where the sick and wounded were treated.
